items.informal_name: Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that takes a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and another natural number $m$, returning a natural number used to establish well-founded recursion in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem. It computes bounds by recursively applying $f$ to $n$ and decrementing $m$.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Successor Case for Numerical Bound in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type:
∀ (k₀ k : ℕ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ),
  ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k₀ (fun x => Nat.casesOn x k D) (n + 1) =
    ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound (k₀ * k) ((k₀ * k) ^ (k₀ * k) • D) n
items.informal_description: For natural numbers $k_0, k, n$ and function $D : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the numerical bound for $n+1$ satisfies: $$\text{numBound}(k_0, \text{casesOn}(k, D), n+1) = \text{numBound}(k_0 \cdot k, (k_0 \cdot k)^{k_0 \cdot k} \bullet D, n)$$ where $\bullet$ denotes natural scalar multiplication of functions.

items.informal_name: Schwartz-Zippel Lemma: Root Bound via Supremum of Exponent Ratios
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [inst_2 : DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R},
  p ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (S : Fin n → Finset R),
      ↑{x ∈ Fintype.piFinset fun i => S i | (MvPolynomial.eval x) p = 0}.card / ∏ i, ↑(S i).card ≤
        p.support.sup fun s => ∑ i, ↑(s i) / ↑(S i).card
items.informal_description: For any non-zero multivariate polynomial $ p $ in $ n $ variables over a commutative semiring $ R $, and for any finite subsets $ S_i \subseteq R $ for each variable, the ratio of the number of roots of $ p $ in the product set $ S_1 \times \cdots \times S_n $ to the product of the cardinalities $ \prod_{i=1}^n |S_i| $ is at most the supremum over all monomials $ s $ in the support of $ p $ of the sum $ \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{s_i}{|S_i|} $, where $ s_i $ denotes the exponent of the $ i $-th variable in the monomial $ s $. All divisions are performed in the non-negative rational numbers $ \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0} $.

items.informal_name: Numerical Bound for Chevalley's Theorem in Multivariate Polynomials with Multiset Counts
items.type: ℕ → (m : ℕ) → ℕ → Multiset (Fin m) → ℕ
items.informal_description: A function that computes a numerical bound used in the context of Chevalley's theorem for multivariate polynomials. It takes natural numbers $k$, $m$, $n$ and a multiset $d$ of elements of type $\text{Fin}\, m$, and returns a natural number obtained by applying the multivariate polynomial bound function to $k + n$ and a function that counts the occurrences of each element in the multiset $d$ after mapping each element to its value in $\mathbb{N}$, then adding 1.
